title: Allergen Labelling and Natasha's Law
welcome_lead: October 2021 — every prepacked-for-direct-sale food must list ingredients.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: allergen labelling, FIC 2014, Natasha's Law 2021.

concepts.def: Substance triggering immune reaction (peanut, gluten, dairy).
UK/EU list requiring labelling under FIC.
Food Information for Consumers Regulation (EU 1169/2011, UK 2014).
UK law (Oct 2021) requiring full ingredient labelling on PPDS food.
Prepacked for Direct Sale — packed before order on same premises.

walkthroughs.body_html: UK/EU law lists 14 major allergens requiring labelling: celery, gluten, crustacean, egg, fish, lupin, milk, molluscs, mustard, nuts, peanuts, sesame, soya, sulphites. Must be emphasised in ingredient lists.

Natasha's Law came into force on 1 October 2021, after the death of Natasha Ednan-Laperouse from a Pret baguette in 2016. Requires PPDS food to display name and full ingredient list with allergens emphasised.
Even labelled-allergen-free products can be unsafe via cross-contamination. Separate utensils, segregated storage, colour-coded boards, schedules: HACCP-style control is required.
